question: Who among the following became India’s 76th Chess Grandmaster in the year 2022?
option_3: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Hari'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARI.TTF') format('truetype');} @font-face { font-family: 'Harikris'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARIKRIS.TTF') format('truetype');} </style>Pentala Harikrishna
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pranav Anand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pranav Anand, a teenager from Bengaluru, became India's 76th Chess Grandmaster in September 2022 after completing his final GM norm at the World Youth Chess Championship in Mamaia, Romania. (भारत के 76वें शतरंज ग्रैंडमास्टर)

 

• He earned the Grandmaster title following a strong run of GM-norm performances, joining the rapidly growing list of young Indian chess prodigies.

 

• To become a Grandmaster, a player must earn three GM norms and cross an Elo rating of 2500, with the title awarded by FIDE (the International Chess Federation).

 

• India's chess strength has grown rapidly in recent years, producing several teenage Grandmasters such as R Praggnanandhaa, D Gukesh and Nihal Sarin.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Viswanathan Anand was India's first Grandmaster, achieving the title in 1988, and remains a five-time World Chess Champion.

 

• D Gukesh and R Praggnanandhaa are among India's other prominent young Grandmasters who rose to prominence around the same period.

 

NOTE

 

• Viswanathan Anand (Option 1): India's first Grandmaster (1988) and a five-time World Chess Champion; he was not the 76th GM.

 

• Pentala Harikrishna (Option 3): An established Indian Grandmaster who earned his title in 2001, long before 2022.

 

• Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa (Option 4): Became a Grandmaster in 2018 at the age of 12, not in 2022.

question: Who among the following was the first-ever badminton player from India to clinch an Olympic medal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saina Nehwal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saina Nehwal became the first Indian badminton player to win an Olympic medal, claiming bronze at the 2012 London Olympics. (भारत की पहली ओलंपिक पदक विजेता बैडमिंटन खिलाड़ी)

 

• She later became the first Indian woman to reach the World No. 1 ranking in badminton, in 2015.

 

• PV Sindhu followed her, winning silver at the 2016 Rio Olympics and bronze at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Saina Nehwal has also won a bronze medal at the World Championships and multiple Commonwealth and Asian Games medals.

 

• India's badminton medal tally at the Olympics currently stands at three medals — all won by Saina Nehwal and PV Sindhu.

 

NOTE

 

• Srikanth Kidambi (Option 1): A former World No. 1 men's singles player and World Championship silver medallist (2017), but has no Olympic medal.

 

• Chirag Shetty (Option 3): Part of India's successful men's doubles pair with Satwiksairaj Rankireddy; has not won an Olympic medal.

 

• PV Sindhu (Option 4): India's most decorated Olympic badminton player with two medals, but she is not the first — that distinction belongs to Saina Nehwal.

question: Which of the following disease is caused by fungi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ring Worm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ring Worm (Dermatophytosis) is a common fungal infection of the skin caused by dermatophyte fungi, appearing as a circular, itchy rash. (फफूंद जनित रोग)

 

• Fungal diseases in humans also include Athlete's Foot, Candidiasis and Aspergillosis.

 

• Fungi reproduce mainly through spores and thrive in warm, moist environments, which is why skin folds are commonly affected.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Antifungal creams and drugs like clotrimazole and terbinafine are commonly used to treat ringworm.

 

• The study of fungi is called mycology, and diseases caused by fungi are called mycoses.

 

NOTE

 

• Covid-19 (Option 1): Caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, not a fungus.

 

• Tuberculosis (Option 3): Caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

 

• Cholera (Option 4): Caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae.

question: The city of Fatehpur Sikri was built by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Akbar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The city of Fatehpur Sikri, near Agra, was built by the Mughal emperor Akbar starting in 1571, to commemorate the birth of his son (later Jahangir) as blessed by Sufi saint Salim Chishti. (फतेहपुर सीकरी — अकबर द्वारा निर्मित)

 

• It served as the capital of the Mughal Empire from 1571 to 1585, after which it was largely abandoned, mainly due to water scarcity.

 

• Notable structures there include the Buland Darwaza, Jama Masjid, Panch Mahal and the tomb of Salim Chishti.

 

• Fatehpur Sikri is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognised for its outstanding Mughal architecture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Buland Darwaza, built to commemorate Akbar's victory over Gujarat, is one of the tallest gateways in the world.

 

• Akbar's reign (1556-1605) is also noted for religious tolerance and the policy of Sulh-i-Kul.

 

NOTE

 

• Aurangzeb (Option 2): The last major Mughal emperor, known for expanding the empire and orthodox religious policies; did not build Fatehpur Sikri.

 

• Shah Jahan (Option 3): Known for building the Taj Mahal, Red Fort and Jama Masjid in Delhi.

 

• Jahangir (Option 4): Akbar's son and successor, born at Fatehpur Sikri, but not its builder.

question: How many silver medals did Indian athletes win in the 2022 Commonwealth Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 16.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India finished 4th in the medal tally at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, held in Birmingham, England, winning a total of 61 medals. (2022 राष्ट्रमंडल खेल — भारत की पदक तालिका)

 

• The break-up was 22 Gold, 16 Silver and 23 Bronze medals.

 

• Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu won India's first gold of the Games, while wrestlers and table tennis players also contributed heavily to the medal tally.

 

• India's contingent excelled particularly in wrestling, weightlifting, table tennis and badminton at these Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2022 Commonwealth Games were held without shooting as a discipline, which affected India's traditionally strong medal count in that sport.

 

• The next Commonwealth Games is scheduled to be held in Glasgow, Scotland, in 2026.

 

NOTE

 

• 14 (Option 1): Understates India's actual silver medal count of 16.

 

• 18 (Option 2): Overstates India's actual silver medal count.

 

• 20 (Option 3): Overstates India's actual silver medal count; India's bronze tally was 23, not its silver tally.

question: What is the approximate literacy rate of India as per the 2011 census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 74.04 percent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the 2011 Census, India's literacy rate was approximately 74.04% (male: 82.14%, female: 65.46%). (2011 जनगणना — भारत की साक्षरता दर)

 

• Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate among states, while Bihar recorded the lowest.

 

• The 2011 Census was the 15th Census of India and the 7th after independence, and was conducted with the tagline 'Our Census, Our Future'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's literacy rate has risen steadily from about 18.33% in 1951 to 74.04% in 2011.

 

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

 

NOTE

 

• 70.01 percent (Option 1): Not the actual 2011 Census figure; understates the correct value.

 

• 78.2 percent (Option 2): Overstates India's actual 2011 literacy rate.

 

• 83.35 percent (Option 4): Overstates India's actual 2011 literacy rate.

question: At which Indian institution did President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu, inaugurate 'PARAM KAMRUPA' Supercomputer facility in October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is IIT Guwahati.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• President Droupadi Murmu inaugurated the 'PARAM KAMRUPA' Supercomputer facility at IIT Guwahati in October 2022, during her visit to Assam. (भारत की राष्ट्रपति — परम कामरूप सुपर कंप्यूटर)

 

• PARAM KAMRUPA was set up under the National Supercomputing Mission (NSM), a joint initiative of the Ministry of Electronics and IT and the Department of Science and Technology.

 

• During the same visit, she also inaugurated a laboratory for high-power microwave components at IIT Guwahati and laid foundation stones for medical facilities in Assam.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Supercomputing Mission aims to establish a network of supercomputing facilities across major institutions in India.

 

• Other PARAM series supercomputers include PARAM Siddhi-AI, PARAM Shakti and PARAM Ganga, installed at various IITs.

 

NOTE

 

• University of Mumbai (Option 2): Not the site of the PARAM KAMRUPA inauguration.

 

• IIT Kharagpur (Option 3): Hosts the PARAM Shakti supercomputer, not PARAM KAMRUPA.

 

• NIT Warangal (Option 4): Not associated with the PARAM KAMRUPA facility.

question: The S-400 Triumf (Russian for Triumph) Missile System is ______ missile defense system designed in Russia.
solution_text:
The correct answer is surface-to-air.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The S-400 Triumf is a surface-to-air missile (SAM) system designed by Russia's Almaz-Antey, capable of engaging aircraft, drones and ballistic/cruise missiles. (सतह से हवा में मार करने वाली मिसाइल प्रणाली)

 

• It can track multiple targets simultaneously and engage them at ranges of up to 400 km, at altitudes up to 30 km.

 

• India signed a deal to procure the S-400 system from Russia in 2018, and deliveries began in 2021-22, despite the threat of US sanctions under CAATSA.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has named its S-400 squadrons 'Sudarshan Chakra'.

 

• The S-400 is considered one of the most advanced air defence systems in the world, alongside the US Patriot and THAAD systems.

 

NOTE

 

• air-to-underwater (Option 1): Not a recognised missile defense category; irrelevant to the S-400.

 

• surface-to-surface (Option 3): Describes missiles like Agni or Prithvi, not the S-400 air defense system.

 

• air-to-air (Option 4): Describes missiles fired from aircraft at other aircraft, not the S-400.

question: A type of loan that allows borrowers to make low payments in the initial phases but repayment of the balance amount in lump sum at maturity is known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Balloon Mortgage.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Balloon Mortgage is a type of loan where the borrower makes low (or interest-only) payments for an initial period, followed by one large lump-sum ('balloon') payment of the remaining balance at maturity. (गुब्बारा बंधक — प्रारंभ में कम भुगतान, अंत में एकमुश्त भुगतान)

 

• These loans are typically short-term (5-7 years) and carry the risk that the borrower may need to refinance or sell the asset to make the final large payment.

 

• They differ from a standard fully amortizing mortgage, where equal payments over the loan's life pay off both principal and interest completely.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Balloon mortgages are often used in commercial real estate financing.

 

• A payday loan is a very different, short-term, high-interest loan meant to be repaid by the borrower's next paycheque, not a low-initial-payment mortgage structure.

 

NOTE

 

• English Mortgage (Option 2): A mortgage type under Indian law (Transfer of Property Act) where the borrower binds to repay on a certain date and transfers the property absolutely, to be re-transferred on repayment.

 

• Income - Sensitive Payment (Option 3): A repayment plan (mainly for student loans) where payments are based on the borrower's income, not a lump-sum-at-maturity structure.

 

• Payday Loans (Option 4): Short-term, high-interest loans meant to be repaid quickly from the borrower's next salary, not loans with deferred lump-sum repayment.

question: Which among the following is a unit of measurement that describes the rate at which the universe is expanding?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hubble constant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hubble constant (H₀) is the unit of measurement that describes the rate at which the universe is expanding, expressed in km/s per megaparsec. (हबल स्थिरांक — ब्रह्मांड के विस्तार की दर)

 

• It is named after astronomer Edwin Hubble, who in 1929 discovered that galaxies are moving away from us at a speed proportional to their distance — the basis of Hubble's Law.

 

• The Hubble constant is central to estimating the age of the universe and is measured using data from telescopes such as the Hubble Space Telescope.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Current estimates of the Hubble constant are roughly 67-73 km/s/Mpc, with different measurement methods giving slightly different values (the "Hubble tension").

 

• The discovery of the universe's expansion later contributed to the development of the Big Bang theory of cosmic origin.

 

NOTE

 

• Faraday constant (Option 1): Relates to electric charge per mole of electrons, used in electrochemistry.

 

• Planck's constant (Option 2): A fundamental constant in quantum mechanics relating a photon's energy to its frequency.

 

• Electric constant (Option 3): Also called the permittivity of free space, it relates to electric fields in a vacuum, not cosmic expansion.

question: Which political organization was banned in September 2022 by Government of India under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Popular Front of India (PFI).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In September 2022, the Government of India banned the Popular Front of India (PFI) and its associate organisations for five years under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), 1967. (गैरकानूनी गतिविधियां (रोकथाम) अधिनियम)

 

• The ban followed allegations that PFI had links to extremist activities and was found to be a threat to internal security and public order.

 

• The UAPA is India's primary anti-terror law, empowering the government to declare an organisation "unlawful" or a "terrorist organisation."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• PFI was formed in 2006 in Kerala and later expanded operations to several other states.

 

• Along with PFI, its affiliates such as the Rehab India Foundation, Campus Front of India and National Confederation of Human Rights Organisation were also banned.

 

NOTE

 

• Khalistan Zindabad Force (Option 1): A separate Sikh separatist militant outfit, also banned under UAPA, but in a different action.

 

• All Tripura Tiger Force (Option 3): A banned insurgent group operating in Tripura, unrelated to the September 2022 PFI ban.

 

• Jammu and Kashmir Islamic Front (Option 4): A banned Kashmir-based militant organisation, not the group banned specifically in this action.

question: Which country's space agency has launched project “DART Mission”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is USA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) Mission was launched by the USA's NASA, and it successfully impacted the asteroid moonlet Dimorphos on 26 September 2022. (नासा का डबल एस्टरॉइड पुनर्निर्देशन परीक्षण मिशन)

 

• It was the world's first planetary defense test mission, demonstrating the kinetic impactor technique to alter an asteroid's trajectory.

 

• The mission successfully shortened Dimorphos's orbital period around its parent asteroid Didymos, proving the technique could work to deflect a potentially hazardous asteroid.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• DART was launched in November 2021 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket.

 

• The European Space Agency's follow-up mission, Hera, was launched later to study the aftermath of the DART impact in detail.

 

NOTE

 

• Russia (Option 2): Its space agency Roscosmos was not involved in the DART mission.

 

• India (Option 3): ISRO was not involved in the DART mission.

 

• China (Option 4): CNSA was not involved in the DART mission.

question: In ______, Ambedkar started a temple entry movement, in which his Mahar caste followers participated.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1927.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1927, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar led the Mahad Satyagraha at Mahad in Maharashtra, asserting the right of the "untouchable" Mahar community to draw water from the public Chavdar Tank, a movement associated with his broader civil and temple-entry rights agitation of the period. (डॉ. अंबेडकर — महाड़ सत्याग्रह, 1927)

 

• As part of this agitation, Ambedkar and his followers also attempted to enter the nearby Veereshwar Temple, marking an early assertion of temple-entry rights by the Mahar community.

 

• Ambedkar later led a more famous, dedicated temple-entry movement at the Kalaram Temple, Nashik, beginning in 1930, separately known as the Kalaram Mandir Satyagraha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mahad Satyagraha is regarded as the starting point of the organised Dalit rights movement in India.

 

• Ambedkar publicly burned copies of the Manusmriti during the Mahad Satyagraha in December 1927, symbolising rejection of caste-based scriptures.

 

NOTE

 

• 1923 (Option 1): Not the year associated with this movement.

 

• 1925 (Option 3): Not a year linked to this specific movement.

 

• 1921 (Option 4): Ambedkar was still pursuing his doctoral studies abroad around this time, before his major activism in India began.

question: What is the public healthcare spending percentage as GDP of India, as per Economic Survey 2020-21?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Economic Survey 2020-21, India's public (government) healthcare spending stood at around 1% of GDP, one of the lowest levels among major economies. (भारत का सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य व्यय — सकल घरेलू उत्पाद का लगभग 1%)

 

• The Survey strongly recommended increasing public health expenditure to 2.5-3% of GDP, in line with the target set by the National Health Policy, 2017.

 

• The Survey, prepared under the Chief Economic Adviser, highlighted that even a modest increase in public health spending could substantially reduce out-of-pocket expenditure by citizens.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Economic Survey is presented in Parliament a day before the Union Budget, giving an overview of the economy's performance and policy recommendations.

 

• India's low public health spending has historically pushed a large share of healthcare costs onto households as out-of-pocket expenses.

 

NOTE

 

• 2.5% (Option 1): This is the target recommended by the Economic Survey/National Health Policy, not the actual spending level at the time.

 

• 4.5% (Option 3): Far higher than India's actual public health expenditure.

 

• 5.5% (Option 4): Far higher than India's actual public health expenditure.

question: Which Indian was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in the year 1930?
solution_text:
The correct answer is C. V. Raman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sir C. V. Raman was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for his discovery of the "Raman Effect" — the scattering of light when it passes through a transparent medium, changing its wavelength. (सी. वी. रमन — रमन प्रभाव)

 

• He remains the only Indian to win a Nobel Prize in a science category while working in India, and the discovery was made using indigenous equipment.

 

• National Science Day is celebrated on 28 February every year in India to commemorate the announcement of the Raman Effect in 1928.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• C. V. Raman founded the Indian Academy of Sciences and later the Raman Research Institute in Bengaluru.

 

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954, India's highest civilian honour.

 

NOTE

 

• Vikram Sarabhai (Option 1): Known as the "Father of the Indian Space Programme"; did not win a Nobel Prize.

 

• Rabindranath Tagore (Option 3): Won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913, not Physics.

 

• Amartya Sen (Option 4): Won the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences in 1998, not Physics.

question: Which of the following statement regarding ocean currents is correct?
option_1: The Labrador Ocean current is warm current.
option_2: The areas where the warm and cold currents meet provide the best fishing grounds.
option_3: The cold ocean currents move towards the poles.
option_4: The warm ocean currents move towards the equator.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The areas where the warm and cold currents meet provide the best fishing grounds.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Where warm and cold ocean currents converge, nutrient-rich cold waters mix with warmer waters, creating ideal conditions for plankton growth, which in turn attracts large fish populations — making these areas the world's best fishing grounds. (गर्म और ठंडी धाराओं का मिलन क्षेत्र — सर्वश्रेष्ठ मत्स्यन क्षेत्र)

 

• A classic example is the Grand Banks off Newfoundland, where the warm Gulf Stream meets the cold Labrador Current.

 

• Similarly, off the coast of Japan, the warm Kuroshio Current meeting the cold Oyashio Current creates rich fishing grounds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Warm ocean currents generally flow from the equator towards the poles, while cold currents flow from the poles towards the equator — the reverse of what Options 3 and 4 state.

 

• Ocean currents play a major role in regulating regional and global climate, e.g., the Gulf Stream keeps Western Europe relatively warm.

 

NOTE

 

• The Labrador Ocean current is warm current (Option 1): Incorrect — the Labrador Current is a cold current flowing from the Arctic along Canada's east coast.

 

• The cold ocean currents move towards the poles (Option 3): Incorrect — cold currents move from the poles towards the equator.

 

• The warm ocean currents move towards the equator (Option 4): Incorrect — warm currents move from the equator towards the poles.

question: Which among the following is a database software?
solution_text:
The correct answer is dBase.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• dBase was one of the earliest and most popular database management system (DBMS) software, originally released for CP/M and later MS-DOS/Windows systems. (डेटाबेस सॉफ्टवेयर)

 

• It allowed users to create, manage, and query structured data using its own programming language, and greatly influenced later database software.

 

• Database software is used to store, organize, retrieve and manage data efficiently, unlike word processors or presentation tools.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known database software includes MS Access, Oracle, MySQL, and SQL Server.

 

• dBase was developed by Ashton-Tate and was one of the best-selling software titles of the 1980s.

 

NOTE

 

• MS-PowerPoint (Option 1): A presentation software used to create slideshows, not a database tool.

 

• MS-Word (Option 2): A word-processing software used for documents, not a database tool.

 

• Word Pad (Option 4): A basic text editor bundled with Windows, not a database tool.

question: Which among the following Indian cities received World Green City Award 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hyderabad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hyderabad won the 'World Green City Award 2022' at the AIPH (International Association of Horticultural Producers) World Green City Awards, becoming the only Indian city to receive this honour that year. (हैदराबाद — विश्व हरित शहर पुरस्कार 2022)

 

• The award recognised Hyderabad's initiatives under its urban greening programme, including large-scale tree plantation drives and the development of urban parks and green spaces.

 

• Hyderabad was also separately recognised as one of the world's "Tree Cities of the World" by the Arbor Day Foundation and the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The AIPH World Green City Awards recognise cities globally for excellence in green infrastructure across categories like health & wellbeing, economic recovery, and biodiversity.

 

• Telangana's "Haritha Haram" is a major afforestation programme that has contributed to Hyderabad's green initiatives.

 

NOTE

 

• New Delhi (Option 1): Did not receive the World Green City Award 2022.

 

• Mumbai (Option 3): Did not receive the World Green City Award 2022.

 

• Pune (Option 4): Did not receive the World Green City Award 2022.

question: Article 143 of the Indian constitution is related with which of the following?
option_1: Power of the President to enlarge jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
option_2: Power of the President to consult the Supreme Court
option_3: Power of the President to appoint National Judicial Appointments Commission
option_4: Power of the President to transfer certain cases from High Courts to Supreme Court
solution_text:
The correct answer is Power of the President to consult the Supreme Court.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 143 of the Indian Constitution grants the President the power to seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court on questions of law or fact of public importance. (राष्ट्रपति की सर्वोच्च न्यायालय से परामर्श की शक्ति)

 

• This is known as the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court; however, the Court's opinion given under this Article is not binding on the President.

 

• Notable instances where Article 143 has been invoked include the Ayodhya reference (1993) and the Presidential Reference on the 2G spectrum case (2012).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 143 is part of Chapter IV of Part V of the Constitution, dealing with the Union Judiciary.

 

• The advisory jurisdiction under Article 143 is distinct from the Supreme Court's original, appellate, and writ jurisdictions.

 

NOTE

 

• Power of the President to enlarge jurisdiction of the Supreme Court (Option 1): This power is provided under Article 138, not Article 143.

 

• Power of the President to appoint National Judicial Appointments Commission (Option 3): The NJAC was a proposed body (via the 99th Amendment) later struck down by the Supreme Court in 2015; unrelated to Article 143.

 

• Power of the President to transfer certain cases from High Courts to Supreme Court (Option 4): This power is provided under Article 139A, not Article 143.

question: Article 72 of the Indian constitution is related with the power of the ______ to grant pardons, etc. and to suspend, remit or commute sentences in certain cases.
solution_text:
The correct answer is President.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 72 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President of India to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment, and to suspend, remit or commute sentences in certain cases, including death sentences and court-martial punishments. (राष्ट्रपति की क्षमादान शक्ति)

 

• This power is broader than the Governor's pardoning power under Article 161, as only the President can pardon a death sentence or sentences by court-martial.

 

• The pardoning power is exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers, and is subject to judicial review in cases of arbitrariness.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Forms of clemency under Article 72 include pardon, commutation, remission, respite, and reprieve.

 

• The President's pardoning power under Article 72 and the Governor's under Article 161 are frequently compared in constitutional law questions.

 

NOTE

 

• Chief Minister (Option 1): Has no constitutional pardoning power under Article 72.

 

• Governor (Option 2): Has a separate, narrower pardoning power under Article 161, which excludes death sentences.

 

• Prime Minister (Option 4): Has no constitutional pardoning power; the Council of Ministers headed by the PM only advises the President.

question: When did Indigo revolt, a peasant movement, start in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1859.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indigo Revolt began in 1859 in Bengal, when indigo cultivators (ryots) refused to grow indigo under the exploitative system imposed by European planters. (नील विद्रोह — 1859)

 

• The revolt was triggered by the coercive practices of planters, who forced peasants into unfair contracts and paid extremely low prices for indigo.

 

• The movement was supported by Bengali intellectuals, and events were dramatised in Dinabandhu Mitra's play "Nil Darpan" (1860), which brought national attention to the plight of indigo farmers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indigo Commission was set up by the British government in 1860 to investigate the grievances, eventually leading to some reforms.

 

• The Champaran Satyagraha (1917), led by Mahatma Gandhi, addressed a similar exploitative indigo cultivation system in Bihar.

 

NOTE

 

• 1857 (Option 1): The year of the Revolt of 1857 (First War of Independence), not the Indigo Revolt.

 

• 1861 (Option 2): After the actual start of the Indigo Revolt in 1859.

 

• 1889 (Option 4): Decades after the actual Indigo Revolt.

question: What is the official language of Bhutan, a neighbouring country of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dzongkha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dzongkha is the official and national language of Bhutan, a Himalayan neighbour of India. (भूटान की राष्ट्रभाषा — जोंगखा)

 

• It is written in the Tibetan script and is spoken predominantly in western Bhutan, while several other languages/dialects are spoken across the country.

 

• Bhutan's currency is the Ngultrum, which is pegged to the Indian Rupee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhutan is the only country in the world that measures development through "Gross National Happiness (GNH)" instead of just GDP.

 

• Bhutan's capital is Thimphu, and it shares its northern border with China (Tibet) and its southern, eastern and western borders with India.

 

NOTE

 

• Kyat (Option 1): The official currency of Myanmar, not the language of Bhutan.

 

• Yuan (Option 3): The official currency of China, not the language of Bhutan.

 

• Ngultrum (Option 4): The official currency (not language) of Bhutan.

question: What is the zone between the arctic circle and north pole called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Frigid zone.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Frigid zone is the region between the Arctic Circle (66.5° N) and the North Pole (90° N) — as well as the corresponding region between the Antarctic Circle and the South Pole in the southern hemisphere. (हिमशीत कटिबंध)

 

• These zones receive the least amount of direct sunlight due to the high angle of incidence, resulting in extremely cold climates.

 

• The Earth's surface is broadly divided into the Torrid Zone (between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn), the Temperate Zones (between the tropics and polar circles), and the Frigid Zones (poleward of the polar circles).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Frigid zones experience continuous daylight (midnight sun) or continuous darkness for parts of the year, due to Earth's axial tilt.

 

• The North Frigid Zone includes parts of Greenland, northern Canada, and Arctic Russia.

 

NOTE

 

• Torrid zone (Option 1): Lies between the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn, receiving the most direct sunlight.

 

• North temperate zone (Option 3): Lies between the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle, not beyond the Arctic Circle.

 

• South temperate zone (Option 4): Lies between the Tropic of Capricorn and the Antarctic Circle, in the southern hemisphere.

question: Sir Tim Berners-Lee — a British computer scientist invented the revolutionary World Wide Web in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1990.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sir Tim Berners-Lee, a British computer scientist working at CERN, invented the World Wide Web in 1990, building the first web browser, web server, and the first webpage. (वर्ल्ड वाइड वेब के आविष्कारक)

 

• He had earlier proposed the idea in a 1989 memo titled "Information Management: A Proposal," but it was in 1990 that he wrote the code implementing HTML, HTTP and URLs, laying the actual technical foundation of the Web.

 

• The first website went live to the public in 1991, and the Web was made royalty-free for anyone to use in 1993, driving its rapid global adoption.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tim Berners-Lee was knighted in 2004 for his services to the global development of the internet.

 

• He later founded the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) to oversee the Web's continued development and standards.

 

NOTE

 

• 1982 (Option 1): Predates any of Berners-Lee's Web-related work.

 

• 1995 (Option 2): Well after the Web had already been invented and popularised.

 

• 1985 (Option 4): Predates Berners-Lee's invention of the World Wide Web.

question: How many Vedas are there in Indian literature of classical Hinduism?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Four.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• There are four Vedas in classical Hinduism: the Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda. (चार वेद — ऋग्वेद, यजुर्वेद, सामवेद, अथर्ववेद)

 

• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four and consists mainly of hymns dedicated to various deities.

 

• The Samaveda is largely derived from the Rigveda and is set to musical chants, while the Yajurveda contains ritual formulas, and the Atharvaveda contains hymns, spells and everyday charms.

 

• Each Veda traditionally comprises four parts: Samhitas (hymns), Brahmanas (rituals), Aranyakas (philosophical texts), and Upanishads (metaphysical texts).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vedas are considered "Shruti" (revealed/heard) texts, as opposed to "Smriti" (remembered) texts like the Puranas and epics.

 

• The Vedas were composed in Vedic Sanskrit and transmitted orally for centuries before being written down.

 

NOTE

 

• Three (Option 1): Undercounts the Vedas; there are four, not three.

 

• One (Option 3): Undercounts the Vedas significantly.

 

• Two (Option 4): Undercounts the Vedas; there are four, not two.
